body_markdown:
After years of rumors and speculation,[the next Mitsubishi Montero](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/spotted-mitsubishi-montero-successor/) is around the corner. The long-awaited SUV was developed as a true off-roader with body-on-frame construction and cool heritage-laced features, and it will make its debut in early September. But while the model is making a comeback in numerous global markets, Mitsubishi hasn’t confirmed it for the American market.


Spy shots[taken in Europe](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/spotted-mitsubishi-montero-successor/) show the outline of a boxy, rugged-looking SUV that looks big enough to offer three rows of seats. The psychedelic camouflage does a good job of covering up the finer design details, but one of Mitsubishi’s preview images reveals that the front end gets horizontal LED lights that stretch across the grille. The truck won’t be retro, but it’s old-school in some ways.


The next Montero, which will also be sold as the Pajero or the Shogun in global markets, will notably receive a digital version of the multi-information display available in[earlier models](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/mitsubishis-second-gen-montero-isnt-collector-grade-yet-but-thats-a-good-thing/) . The read-out will provide details such as the outside temperature, the altitude, as well as the roll and pitch angles. It looks like the feature will be integrated into the infotainment system’s touchscreen.


Mitsubishi


Mitsubishi


It’s too early to provide technical details. All we know at this stage is that the next-gen Montero will ride on a body-on-frame platform, so it should offer genuine off-road capability. Thankfully, Mitsubishi resisted the urge to turn it into a car-based crossover. We don’t know which engines it will be available with yet, but we wouldn’t be surprised if the specifications sheet includes a hybrid option.


The next Mitsubishi Montero will[make its public debut](https://www.mitsubishi-motors.co.jp/global/en/lineup/pajero/teaser/) on September 2, 2026. When it lands, the model will reinstate Mitsubishi within a segment that it abandoned years ago. The nameplate retired from the American market in 2006, and it left the global catalog in 2021. Meanwhile, rivals like[the Toyota Land Cruiser](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/first-drive-review-2024-toyota-land-cruiser-is-one-for-the-die-hards/) have benefited from the market’s strong appetite for off-roading SUVs.


Beyond the Land Cruiser, the next Montero will need to fend off competition from[the Nissan Armada](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/first-drive-the-2026-armada-nismo-brings-more-power-and-exuberance-to-nissans-full-size-suv/) , which is known as the Patrol in numerous global markets. And, in an odd twist of fate, the segment could soon grow to include[a new Volkswagen SUV](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/volkswagen-body-on-frame-suv-report/) .


We’ll need to be patient to find out whether the Montero returns to American showrooms:


“While one of the key pillars of our Momentum 2030 business plan is the debut of at least one all-new or extensively revised vehicle each year between now and 2030, we have nothing to say at this time about whether or not the new Pajero (Montero) will be one of the models in the plan,” a Mitsubishi spokesperson told us via email.
